conventions.coordinates: 0-based half-open on the TOP strand for both strands. backend/routers/analysis.py:112 documents ORF.start as '0-based position on input strand'; a negative-frame ORF reported [start, end) is read as reverse_complement(sequence[start:end]).
conventions.frames: +1/+2/+3 read sequence[offset:] for offset 0/1/2; -1/-2/-3 read reverse_complement(sequence)[offset:]. A span [s, e) in reverse-strand space is [n - e, n - s) on the top strand.
conventions.initiator: The reported `protein` renders the initiator as M whatever the start codon codes for elsewhere -- the GenBank /translation convention. Every requirement below that compares a protein to a literal translation compares protein[1:] against translation[1:] and says so.
conventions.stop_in_span: For a complete ORF the reported span INCLUDES the terminating stop codon, so length_nt == 3 * (length_aa + 1). Established by OR-5, not assumed.

requirements.statement: backend.routers.analysis.GENETIC_CODE is NCBI translation table 1, exactly: all 64 codons present, each mapping to the amino acid gc.prt's ncbieaa string gives for that codon, with '*' at TAA, TAG and TGA and nothing else.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt#ncbieaa, cross-checked against gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Data/CodonTable.py#register_ncbi_table by re-rendering Biopython's table 1 back into the ncbieaa/sncbieaa strings and requiring an exact match.
requirements.oracle: gc.prt, independently of Biopython; the two authorities must first agree with each other.

requirements.statement: Alternative codes change exactly the codons they should and nothing else. Against gc.prt: table 2 (vertebrate mitochondrial) differs from table 1 at exactly four codons -- TGA '*'->'W', ATA 'I'->'M', AGA 'R'->'*', AGG 'R'->'*'; table 11 (bacterial) differs from table 1 at ZERO codons and differs only in its start set, adding GTG, ATT, ATC and ATA. Through the subject: restated_translation on the real MT-CYTB bases of NC_012920.1 with /transl_table=2 and with /transl_table=1 must produce proteins differing at exactly the residue positions whose codon is one of those four, and restated_translation with /transl_table=11 must equal /transl_table=1 residue for residue.
requirements.oracle: gc.prt for the codon sets; index re-derivation of MT-CYTB's codons for the residue positions.

requirements.statement: Every ORF the subject reports in frame f is exactly a segment of Bio.Seq.translate(frame_substring(sequence, f), table=1) at the residue offset the ORF's own coordinates imply -- i.e. translation of a frame equals Biopython's translation of that frame's substring with the same table, not merely a string of the right length.
requirements.oracle: Bio.Seq.translate on the frame substring, plus index arithmetic to locate the ORF within it.

requirements.statement: Reverse-strand frames map back to top-strand coordinates correctly: for every ORF reported with frame in {-1,-2,-3}, reverse_complement(sequence[start:end]) begins with the reported start_codon and, translated, yields the reported protein (modulo the initiator-M convention). The span must round-trip: mapping [start, end) into reverse-strand space and back returns [start, end).
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Seq.py#def reverse_complement; backend/routers/analysis.py:112 for the declared coordinate system.
requirements.oracle: Re-extraction by index from the pinned bases.

requirements.statement: Every reported ORF re-extracts. Slicing the input at [start, end) (reverse-complemented for a negative frame) yields bases whose first three characters are a start codon of the start set in force, whose last three are a table-1 stop codon, and which contain no table-1 stop codon in any interior in-frame position. An ORF that instead runs off the end of the molecule must be flagged as partial rather than reported under the same shape (see OR-9).
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt#ncbieaa (which codons are stops) and #sncbieaa (which are starts).
requirements.oracle: Index re-extraction from the pinned bases plus gc.prt.

requirements.statement: include_all_starts=True draws its start codons from the genetic code in force, not from a free-floating list. gc.prt's sncbieaa for table 1 marks exactly three codons M: ATG, CTG and TTG. So with include_all_starts=True and table 1, a CTG-initiated ORF must be found and a GTG-initiated one must not (GTG is a start in tables 2 and 11, not in table 1).
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt#sncbieaa for table 1; gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Data/CodonTable.py#register_ncbi_table start_codons for table 1.
requirements.oracle: gc.prt, and real CTG-/GTG-initiated frames located by index in the pinned NG_007400.1 bases.

requirements.statement: min_length_aa is honoured exactly and in both directions: no reported ORF is shorter than min_length_aa residues, and every ORF at least that long is reported. Asserted as set equality between the subject's six-frame result and an independent index-walking ORF finder written from the gc.prt definition, over full-length pinned inputs at two thresholds.
requirements.oracle: gx/orf/orf_oracle.find_orfs_oracle -- a second ORF finder written from the definition, not from the subject.

requirements.statement: Every reported ORF is a whole number of codons: end - start == length_nt, and length_nt % 3 == 0. A reported span is a coding interval; it cannot end part-way through a codon.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Seq.py#def translate -- which refuses to treat a non-multiple of three as a complete coding interval, warning 'Partial codon, len(sequence) not a multiple of three'.
requirements.oracle: Arithmetic on the subject's own reported fields; no convention assumed beyond 'a codon is three bases'.

requirements.statement: Partial trailing codons are handled explicitly, not silently. Re-extracting any reported ORF's bases by index and translating them with Bio.Seq.translate must not raise BiopythonWarning('Partial codon'), and an ORF that reaches the end of the molecule without a stop codon must be distinguishable as partial from the result alone -- a consumer must not have to re-derive the bases to learn that the reported protein is unterminated.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Seq.py#Partial codon, len(sequence) not a multiple of three; gx/corpus/inputs/NC_012920.1.gb#/transl_except=(pos:12137,aa:TERM) for the biology -- NCBI itself declares these CDS ends incomplete.
requirements.oracle: Bio.Seq.translate's warning behaviour on the re-extracted bases; the ORF model's own fields for distinguishability.

requirements.statement: RNA input denotes the same molecule as its DNA back-transcription. find_orfs on an RNA sequence must report the same ORFs, at the same coordinates, as find_orfs on the same sequence with U written T -- or refuse the input. It must not return an empty result.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Seq.py#def translate -- Biopython translates T and U identically; gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Data/CodonTable.py#unambiguous_rna_by_id, which registers the same tables over the RNA alphabet.
requirements.oracle: The subject's own answer for the DNA spelling of the identical molecule, which OR-7 has already pinned against an independent finder.

requirements.statement: Layout characters do not move the ORF coordinates. NG_007400.1's bases wrapped at 60 columns with CRLF line endings denote the same 24,544-base molecule: sequence_length must be 24544 and the reported ORF set must be identical to the unwrapped input's. The app states this invariant itself -- backend/sequence_text.py exists precisely because 'every endpoint and GUI call site that analyses the same template box has to agree on which characters are the molecule and which are layout'.
requirements.authority: backend/sequence_text.py#One definition of what a pasted sequence *is* (#86) and backend/sequence_text.py#def normalize_template -- the app's own definition, already applied by the restriction endpoints.
requirements.oracle: normalize_template on the wrapped text, plus the subject's own answer for the unwrapped molecule.

requirements.statement: On a circular molecule the ORF set does not depend on where the record happens to start. pUC19 is a 2686 bp circular plasmid whose bla gene is a complete 286-residue ORF at top-strand [1625:2486) in frame -3. Rotating the origin into the middle of that gene must not lose it: the multiset of reported protein strings must be identical for the unrotated molecule and for rotations of 1700, 2000 and 2400 bases.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/MANIFEST.json#inputs/puc19_L09137.2.txt (GenBank L09137.2, circular) and the app's own Sequence.is_circular, which it carries through every other operation.
requirements.oracle: The subject's own answer for the unrotated molecule; a rotation is the identity on a circle, so no second ORF finder is needed.

requirements.statement: The ORF finder can be asked for a non-standard genetic code. NC_012920.1 declares /transl_table=2 for all 13 of its CDS features; its MT-ND5 gene is one continuous 603-residue reading frame under table 2 but is interrupted by 11 internal TGA codons, which table 2 reads as tryptophan and table 1 reads as stop. Given MT-ND5's bases and table 2, the finder must report one ORF of 603 residues.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/inputs/NC_012920.1.gb#/transl_table=2 and #/translation= for MT-ND5 (603 residues, NCBI's own literal); gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt#ncbieaa for table 2.
requirements.oracle: NCBI's recorded /translation literal, and index re-derivation of the 11 TGA positions.

requirements.statement: restated_translation reproduces NCBI's own protein for every CDS of NC_012920.1: all 13 /translation qualifiers, byte for byte, under the /transl_table=2 each feature declares. This covers the minus strand (MT-ND6, [14148:14673)), six spans that are not a multiple of three because the stop codon is completed post-transcriptionally (MT-ND1, ND2, COX3, ND3, ND4, CYTB), and the initiator-methionine convention (MT-ND2 starts ATT, which gc.prt marks a table-2 start and which NCBI therefore writes M).
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/inputs/NC_012920.1.gb#/translation= -- recorded literals; gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt#sncbieaa for table 2, which marks ATT a start codon (M).

requirements.statement: The translate edit operation handles a trailing partial codon explicitly. POST /sequences/{id}/edit with operation='translate' on a 17-base sequence must either refuse the input or say in its result that a partial trailing codon was dropped. Reporting 'Translated 17 nt -> 5 aa' -- which is arithmetically impossible, 5 residues being 15 bases -- while emitting Biopython's 'Partial codon' warning to a stream a desktop user never reads, is neither.
requirements.authority: gx/corpus/biopython-1.85/Bio/Seq.py#Partial codon, len(sequence) not a multiple of three -- 'Explicitly trim the sequence or add trailing N before translation. This may become an error in future.' backend/services/annotations.py:76 shows the app already knows this ('A trailing partial codon is dropped before translating, which is what Bio.Seq.translate does with it anyway, minus the warning').
requirements.oracle: The warning Bio.Seq.translate raises, captured in-process, against the result the subject reports.
